title: Vanishing of $H_c^0$ on a nonproper curve
statement:
Let $U_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve and let
$\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf
on $U_0$. Then, in the
compactly supported
cohomology of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology],
$H_c^0(U,\mathcal F)=0$.

proof.text: Use the finite-field conventions [d-real-setup] and write $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $B$ a finitely generated $k_0$-algebra. Then $U=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_{k_0}k)$: the tensor product has the universal property of this affine fibre product. The images of the finitely many generators of $B$ generate $B\otimes_{k_0}k$ over $k$, so $U$ is affine of finite type. It is separated: its diagonal on rings is the surjection $(B\otimes k)\otimes_k(B\otimes k)\to B\otimes k$, $b\otimes b'\mapsto bb'$. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] therefore makes $B\otimes k$ Noetherian, hence its affine spectrum is a Noetherian scheme. Finally $U$ is nonempty and connected by geometric connectedness, which by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] tests all field extensions, in particular $k/k_0$.

source.place: Proof: connected geometric curve; explicit affine scalar-extension and Noetherian checks

proof.text: The smooth curve hypothesis is smoothness of relative dimension one over $k_0$ in the curve convention [d-real-setup]. Apply clause (1) of [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] to $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$; $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth of relative dimension one. Since $U$ is nonempty, [lem-sbc-smooth-fixed-dimension-over-field] gives $\dim U=1$. Applied to this structure morphism, [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] says its fibre over the sole point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, namely $U$ itself, is geometrically reduced; in particular $U$ is reduced. If $U$ were proper, [lem-sc-proper-affine-finite] would make this affine curve finite over $k$, in particular of dimension zero, contrary to $\dim U=1$. Thus $U$ is not proper.

source.place: Tags 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 02NK (lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d); geometry underlying the blueprint support argument

proof.text: Let $c\in H_c^0(U,\mathcal F)$. Apply [lem-a1-degree-zero-compact-support-sections] with $X_0=U_0$; smoothness, separation and finite type were checked above, and $\ell$ is different from the characteristic by the Weil coefficient conventions. It produces the ordinary lisse adic realization $\mathcal L$ and its section $s=\alpha_{U,\mathcal F}(c)$, with $\alpha$ injective. The set $Z$ of underlying points at which the geometric fibre map of $s$ is nonzero is closed, and $Z$ with its reduced induced structure is proper over $k$. This applies to the specified completed/rationalized cohomology, through the comparison asserted in that lemma.

source.place: Definition 18.1, pp. 118-119; Remark 29.7, p. 166; explicit coefficient comparison isolated as a dependency

proof.text: For any geometric point $\bar u$ of $U$, use clause (2) of [cor-galois-lisse-representations]. Its hypotheses hold: $U$ is connected, Noetherian and separated, and $\ell$ is invertible on $U$ because $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. This fibre functor on lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaves is an equivalence and sends the unit to the trivial line. Consequently it is faithful. The section $s$ is a morphism from that unit to $\mathcal L$, so if $s_{\bar u}=0$, faithfulness gives $s=0$. If $s\ne0$, its fibre map is therefore nonzero at every geometric point. Every scheme point admits a geometric point by choosing an algebraic closure of its residue field, so the closed set $Z$ in the preceding step is all of $U$.

source.place: Lemma 7.4.7, Remark 7.4.8 and Lemma 7.4.10; ordinary lisse fibre-equivalence argument, using the previously isolated realization comparison

proof.text: If $s\ne0$, the proper reduced induced subscheme on $Z=U$ is $U$ itself, since $U$ is reduced. This contradicts the nonproperness proved in step 2. Hence $s=0$. Injectivity of $\alpha_{U,\mathcal F}$ now gives $c=0$. As $c$ was arbitrary, $H_c^0(U,\mathcal F)=0$.
